bull.b: The week-100 Phase 2 results provide meaningful clinical validation for ACI-7104, including sustained safety, immunogenicity and cerebrospinal-fluid antibody penetration. These findings support continued development, strengthen the Parkinson’s pipeline, and may improve future partnering potential.

Fast Track status and IND clearance remove important regulatory barriers and enable U.S. expansion of the VacSYn trial. This can support faster interaction with regulators, broaden clinical execution, and improve the program’s strategic relevance within disease-modifying Parkinson’s therapies.

Low debt reduces near-term interest and refinancing pressure while giving AC Immune greater flexibility to direct available resources toward clinical development. Although the company remains loss-making, modest leverage limits one source of financial strain during its pipeline investment period.

bear.b: AC Immune has not yet demonstrated sustainable operating leverage: revenue remains volatile and insufficient to cover the development cost base, while large losses persist. This weakens internally generated funding capacity and keeps financial results dependent on collaborations, milestones, or external capital.

The return to heavy cash consumption means AC Immune may need additional financing or collaboration proceeds to sustain research and clinical programs. Funding requirements can constrain strategic flexibility, particularly if milestone receipts are delayed or partnered development economics change.

The substantial reduction in equity reflects the cumulative impact of losses and leaves a smaller balance-sheet buffer for a capital-intensive clinical-stage business. A thinner cushion increases sensitivity to future funding needs and reduces resilience if development spending remains elevated.
